title: Filter Departments with More Than 2 Employees
description_markdown: Find departments (`dept_id`) that have strictly more than 2 employees. Return `dept_id` and `COUNT(*) AS emp_count`. Exclude NULL `dept_id`. Order by `emp_count` DESC, then `dept_id`.
starter_query:
-- Filter aggregate groups with HAVING
SELECT dept_id, COUNT(*) AS emp_count
FROM employees
WHERE dept_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY dept_id
HAVING ...
solution_query: SELECT dept_id, COUNT(*) AS emp_count FROM employees WHERE dept_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY dept_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 2 ORDER BY emp_count DESC, dept_id ASC;
solution_explanation: The HAVING clause filters grouped rows after aggregation, selecting only groups where `COUNT(*) > 2`.
hints: Use `HAVING COUNT(*) > 2` after `GROUP BY dept_id`.
Focus on the required WHERE, JOIN, or GROUP BY clause conditions.
Query: SELECT dept_id, COUNT(*) AS emp_count FROM employees WHERE dept_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY dept_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 2 ORDER BY emp_count DESC, dept_id ASC;
